speaker: Lawrence Friar
text: Morning, Juliet. You sound awake. That's more than I can say for me.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Ha, I've had two coffees. Morning, Friar. Thanks for keeping the slot.

speaker: Lawrence Friar
text: Of course. So, um, I want to hear about Montague. Benvolio mentioned something at a dinner last week, very vague, and I realized I only know the shape of it.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Yeah, so, we kicked it off yesterday. It's called Schema Bridge. The idea is that inspections from the Balcony App flow straight into Mesh Routing, their routing service, so a warehouse doesn't have to retype anything.

speaker: Lawrence Friar
text: And who's the customer?

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Ducal Freight is the pilot. I've got a call with Paris Duke tomorrow, and Benvolio set up a demo for them on Friday.

speaker: Lawrence Friar
text: Friday. That's quick.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: It is quick. But honestly the kickoff went well. Romeo, he's their staff engineer, he pushed us to send events instead of a nightly batch, and he's prototyping a local queue so Balcony keeps working if Mesh Routing goes down. Tybalt was worried about exactly that.

speaker: Lawrence Friar
text: Good. Tybalt worrying is usually useful. Okay, so here's my one real piece of advice, and then I'll stop being an investor for a minute.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Go ahead.

speaker: Lawrence Friar
text: The shared format. The record that goes back and forth. Who owns it?

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Um. That's the open question, actually. It's literally in my spec under open questions. Who owns field versioning.

speaker: Lawrence Friar
text: Right. So get that written down before Ducal sees a demo. Doesn't have to be a contract, doesn't have to involve lawyers. A page. Who can change the format, who has to agree, what happens when you disagree.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Before Friday, you mean.

speaker: Lawrence Friar
text: Before Friday. Because the moment a customer sees it working, it becomes real. Paris will start asking for changes, and if nobody knows whose format it is, you'll each assume it's yours. That's how nice partnerships get, uh, less nice.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: That's fair. I think Romeo would actually welcome it. He's pretty, like, low-ego about this stuff. Okay. I'll take it to him this week. I'm doing spec v2 by Wednesday anyway, so it can go in there.

speaker: Lawrence Friar
text: Perfect. Now, the boring part. How's runway feeling? I don't need numbers today, I just want the vibe.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: The vibe is fine. We're on plan. Nothing's on fire. If Ducal turns into a paying pilot it gets better, obviously, but we're not counting on it.

speaker: Lawrence Friar
text: Good. Don't count on it, and don't hire ahead of it. Good. Okay, last thing. I've noticed I mostly hear from you when something's either great or terrible.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Oh no. Is that true?

speaker: Lawrence Friar
text: A little. Which is normal, everybody does it. But what I'd love is a short note, weekly. Five bullets. What shipped, what's stuck, one thing I could help with. It takes you ten minutes and it saves us both a meeting now and then.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Yeah, I can do that. Honestly it'd help me too, just to write the week down.

speaker: Lawrence Friar
text: That's the secret. It's mostly for you.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Okay, I'll send the first one Friday. That'll be a good week for it, actually. Balcony 3.0 go or no-go is Friday morning, and the Ducal demo is Friday too.

speaker: Lawrence Friar
text: Alright. Go write your page about who owns the format. I'll look for your note Friday.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Thanks, Friar. Talk soon.
